By HNN Staff Published : Oct. 29, 2026 at 8:25 AM HST | Updated : 34 minutes ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google HONOLULU (HawaiiNewsNow) - Former University of Hawaii Head Football Coach June Jones has passed away at age 73, according to multiple sources on Thursday.
 June Jones was the winningest coach in the modern era of Hawaii football with 76 victories in nine seasons from 1999-2007. He then went to work at Southern Methodist University from 2008 until he resigned in 2014.
 He led UH to six bowl games and coached three 10+-win seasons, including an undefeated 12-0 regular season and trip to the Allstate Sugar Bowl in 2007. His 1999 squad recorded the biggest turnaround in NCAA history with a 9-4 record and share of the Western Athletic Conference title which earned him National Coach of the Year honors. 
 His teams captured two WAC titles (1999 & 2007) and his Run-and-Shoot offense produced record-breaking quarterbacks, most notably Heisman Trophy finalist Colt Brennan. 
 He coached five All-Americans, 52 all-conference performers and 16 NFL Draft picks. A UH quarterback from 1973-74, he also started his coaching career at Hawai‘i as a graduate assistant in 1983.
 Jones agreed to become the next offensive coordinator at Kapolei High School in 2016. 
 He was most recently the offensive coordinator of the Seattle Sea Dragons.
 He coached for three years in the National Football League (NFL). Jones played professionally as a quarterback in the NFL and CFL. He played football with the Oregon Ducks, Rainbow Warriors, and Portland State Vikings
